title: Sources for Gates's five activities ('How to Avoid a Climate Disaster') by sector, all greenhouse gases
need: Gates's book splits the world's 'about 51 billion tons' of greenhouse gases a year into five activities: making things (31%), plugging in (27%), growing things (19%), getting around (16%) and keeping warm and cool (7%), from Rhodium Group data that is proprietary. The site needs an open-licence dataset from the primary producer, all greenhouse gases, for the world and ideally every country as a yearly series, split into sectors fine enough that each maps to exactly one of the five activities or is shown as 'not one of the five' (fuel supply, waste, F-gases, wildfires, natural sinks). The values are regrouped and written to public JSON, so no-derivatives and display-only sources are unusable, and anything built on IEA energy statistics (IEA-EDGAR CO2, IEA World Energy Balances) counts as no-derivatives in this registry. Every regrouped number must keep its subsector-level provenance.

file_urls: https://zenodo.org/api/records/22919723/files/<sector>_<subsector>.zip/content (69 subsector zips, plus fluorinated_gases.zip, ers_plan_global.zip, geometries.gpkg.zip; 71 files, 39,641,394,773 bytes in all; Zenodo gives md5 only, no sha256)

Inside each zip: <gas>/DATA/<subsector>_country_emissions_v5_10_0.csv for gas in co2, ch4, n2o, co2e_100yr, co2e_20yr (plus *_emissions_sources_v5_10_0.csv and *_emissions_sources_confidence_v5_10_0.csv at asset level, monthly from 2021, and ABOUT_THE_DATA/about_the_data_v5_10_0.pdf and detailed_data_schema_v5_10_0.csv)

Country CSV columns: iso3_country, sector, subsector, start_time, end_time, gas, emissions_quantity, emissions_quantity_units (tonnes), temporal_granularity (annual), created_date, modified_date. 3,024 rows each = 252 codes x 12 years (2015-2026; 2026 is a partial year). One file per subsector per gas: there is no single country x sector x gas file.
Each country file can be read without downloading the whole zip (HTTP Range on Zenodo works; road-transportation.zip alone is 4,688,736,120 bytes but its co2e_100yr country CSV is about 0.5 MB)

exclusions.world_size_note: From the live API (v5.11.0), gas=co2e_100yr (AR6 GWP100) and gas=co2 per subsector. Listed subsectors total 11,301 Mt in 2025 = 20.8% of the 54,418 Mt world total (11,295 Mt = 18.9% of 59,912 Mt in 2024). Of that, the IEA-EDGAR CO2 that may not be regrouped is 4,671 Mt (8.6% of 2025); EDGAR's CC BY non-CO2 is 3,397 Mt (mostly F-gases 1,740 and landfill methane 1,084); FAOSTAT (CC BY) is 3,186 Mt with rice counted whole. The EDGAR values are identical in 2024 and 2025: Climate TRACE forward-fills EDGAR from 2022 or 2023. The methodology document 'Data-Informed Disaggregation and Implicit Estimation of Emissions in Other Subsectors' (March 2026) says the EDGAR- or FAOSTAT-based subsectors 'together accounted for approximately 18% of global emissions in 2024'.

evidence: climatetrace.org/data subsector notes (fetched 2026-10-08): road-transportation 'Country level data derived from EDGAR; estimates available from 2015 to 2022.'; residential-onsite-fuel-usage 'Emissions estimates were derived by disaggregating EDGAR Version 8 emissions data using satellite-derived floor area estimates'; non-residential-onsite-fuel-usage 'Data from EDGAR. Estimates available from 2015 to 2022.'; other-chemicals, other-metals, wood-and-wood-products, other-mining-quarrying 'spatially disaggregating country-level CEDS emissions estimates'; glass and lime 'total sectoral emissions within a country using USGS statistics, EDGAR and CEDS'; food-beverage-tobacco and textiles 'UNIDO statistics, EDGAR and CEDS'.

Buildings methodology (github.com/climatetracecoalition/methodology-documents, 2025/Buildings, November 2025): super-resolving EDGAR v8 'ensures the sum of the original EDGAR data is equivalent to the super-resolved dataset at a global and national level'.

Road methodology (2025/Transportation, JHU APL, Fall 2025), section 2.3.7: an activity scale factor of 0.7895 'To better align our estimates with EDGAR v2025' computed from 'annual country level EDGAR v2025 road transportation CO2 emission estimates'.
Heat plants methodology (2025/Power, March 2026): activity from IEA World Energy Balances.
CEDS README (github.com/JGCRI/CEDS): CEDS 'uses open-source data (with the exception of the IEA energy statistics which must be purchased from IEA)'.
unlisted_but_iea_or_edgar_derived.consequence: Together with the listed EDGAR CO2, about 16.4 Gt of the 2025 total (30.2%) has IEA lineage. Road transport (6.8 Gt) and both buildings subsectors (3.6 Gt) are almost all of 'getting around' and 'keeping warm and cool'. Climate TRACE labels them CC BY; this registry's IEA rule would make them no-derivatives. Owner decision and a written question to Climate TRACE are needed (open_questions).

caveats: Modelled estimates, revised every month; pin the Zenodo version, never the API.
Zero is used both for 'not emitted' and, in V5.10.0 2025 land rows, for 'not yet estimated'; the pipeline must treat those as missing, not zero (rule 8).

Climate TRACE's forestry fluxes (fires and natural removals of over 15 Gt) are not comparable with inventories or with Rhodium, which leaves out forest fires; keep them out of the five activities and show them as their own layer.
Asset-level sources and country totals do not reconcile for every subsector (rice: sources 749 Mt vs country 713 Mt in 2024, V5.10.0), so use country files only.
Attribution must credit Climate TRACE and, for listed subsectors, EDGAR (JRC) or FAO; 'indicate if you have made any changes' is required by CC BY.
candidates.recommendation: Use as the only source for the five-activity view, from the pinned Zenodo version, with every subsector carrying a provenance tag. Ingest the Climate TRACE-modelled subsectors as open. For listed EDGAR subsectors ingest only the gas=ch4, n2o and F-gas (co2e) parts as open with EDGAR credited, and leave their gas=co2 parts out (shown as 'IEA-licensed, not shown', a gap of 4.7 Gt). FAOSTAT-sourced subsectors are open with FAO credited. Do not ingest the unlisted EDGAR/CEDS/IEA-derived subsectors until the owner decides (open question 1); without them 'keeping warm and cool' and road transport cannot be shown. Show the shares under the 'strict' mapping by default and say which grouping Rhodium uses.

gates_mapping.rhodium_method_conclusion: No published table maps Rhodium subsectors to the five activities, but Rhodium's own five-sector grouping is the same as Gates's (and Breakthrough Energy's), and its Figure 6 shows the allocation: fossil-fuel production, coal mining and refining go to industry ('making things'), landfills and waste go with agriculture and land use ('growing things'), refrigerant F-gases go to buildings ('keeping warm and cool'), electricity is generation-based (not reallocated to end users), and forest fires are excluded. Shares are of gross emissions with net LULUCF inside agriculture. Rhodium's data are 'All rights reserved' ('No part of the content may be copied ... or redistributed without the prior written consent of Rhodium Group', 2019 and 2024 PDFs) and IEA-based, so they are not usable.

variants.strict: Fuel supply, waste, F-gases, wildfires, natural land fluxes and residual categories are 'not one of the five'. This matches the brief.
variants.rhodium_compatible: Fuel supply -> making things; waste -> growing things; F-gases -> keeping warm and cool; EDGAR residuals other-energy-use -> plugging in, other-onsite-fuel-usage -> keeping warm and cool. Reproduces Gates's split to within about 2 points from Climate TRACE v5.11.0 2025 data (30.1/25.7/20.0/15.3/8.9 against 31/27/19/16/7).

gates_mapping.shares_note: Shares are of the sum of the five activities, not of the world total. Values are Mt CO2e (AR6 GWP100) and include the IEA-lineage subsectors, so they are research checks, not publishable numbers under the current registry rules. Zenodo V5.10.0 2025 land values are distorted by the zero rows noted above.
